title: English bands and thirty-one bands in thirty days
summary: He names Alex Welsh's old players, Humphrey Lyttelton and others, and says on his last tour he played with thirty-one different bands.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, before you leave England, let's talk about the musicians a little bit--

Oh, England--- Well, of course, England is loaded - just loaded with great musicians. And, all those old members of the Alex Welsh Band are now world famous and, of course, it was very unfortunate that the band broke up, but they all gone with the other great bands in England; there's about ten great bands in England and they're known on the continent.

Yeah - for instance, there's Humphrey Littleton's Band now; he has taken some of the members from the Alex Welsh's Band and the Alex Welsh Band is still going; he has taken some of the members of his first

band back. So, those are the two-- when it comes to just traditional and swing-- jazz bands, they are the two top names in Britian; now, there are some other bands there that tour Germany almost constantly. I can't just think of their names off-hand, but they're world famous. One, Midnight Moscow Band - they did that famous record--

I can't think of it, but those guys are working steadily. Now, you see, here's England with hundreds of bands - I just toured England as you know and I played with-- I was there 30 days and I played with 31 different bands.

Yes. And, the only two-- the only time I went to the same band twice was at the Pizza Express-- of course, I get an all-star band for that one, and that was the only two days I stayed in London; the rest of the time I was travelling all over - in Wales and Scotland and, uh, it seems like--- you think when you're travelling around on those fast trains - it's the biggest country in the world - when you have to jump from London to Edinburgh and Glasgow and those places.
